Thanks Evelyn — quick take below. I'm happy to own the quality acceptance with Karthik.

Acceptance (proposed):
- No more than 1.5% overall semantic regression on the promptset (precision-weighted average) vs. baseline over a sliding 24h sample.
- Latency P95 under 320ms for control; P95 under 380ms for treatment (quantized model).
- False-positive hallucination rate under 0.8% on the taxonomy tests.

A/B config: 5% traffic to start (canary), expand to 25% after 48h if metrics stable. Report hourly bins for first 24h, then 6h.

On Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 11:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Evelyn — quick take below. I'm happy to own the quality acceptance with Karthik.

Adding more detail from the evaluation side and gating logic:

Sampling / stats:
- Start 5% traffic (~1k QPS expected combined customers) for 48 hours. Minimum sample for statistical checks = 10k user interactions per cohort.
- Use stratified sampling by region and query-length bucket to avoid bias.

Gates (fail if any):
1) Quality regression: detected semantic delta > 1.5% (as Marissa suggested) with p < 0.05 over the sample window.
2) Hallucination spike: relative increase > 30% vs baseline AND absolute > 0.8%
3) Latency degradation: P95(treatment) - P95(control) > 80ms sustained for 30 minutes
4) Error rate: total error responses > 0.5% for 15m window

Rollback flow:
- Immediate: demote treatment routing, enable fallback to baseline model variant, notify SRE + CS.
- 15m: if errors persist, enable global circuit-break to route 100% to baseline and pause expansion.

Metrics to publish in the dashboard: quality_delta, hallucination_rate, p95_latency, error_rate, cost_delta_per_1k_tokens.

I'll add unit tests to the eval harness for the hallucination taxonomy and link them into the canary pipeline. Owner: Karthik (evals).

-karthik
